messages:
maya: I'm handing off the shift in 5. Primary -> @tom, secondary -> @sasha. Quick summary: we've been paged twice for embeddings p99 latency in eu-west-1 over the last 40m. Incident-bot posted the alert (see below). I'm staying around for 10 minutes to make sure there are no immediate regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: RED-EMB-P99-EU triggered at 2223456600. Severity: P2. Affected: embeddings API (eu-west-1). Link: https://incidents.redwood/2223456600 (pager details).

maya: Customer impact: some latency-sensitive customers (search/embedding lookups) reported >2s tail latencies. No request failures reported, just latency. We've routed traffic to fallback smaller model for a handful of VIP customers to keep UI snappy.

tom: ok taking primary. quick question — is this KV cache thrash or GPU queueing? Any hot keys?

maya: initial digging: KV cache hit-rate dropped ~15% after a spike in long-context jobs. No obvious hot key but a few long prefix requests increased seq length. CPU on router nodes spiked briefly.

liam: FYI I pushed a temporary routing tweak earlier to move non-VIP traffic to dedicated-spot pool to reduce pressure on main pool. Latency improved ~200ms for non-VIP.

maya: thanks @liam — logged the change in the incident timeline. We should include that in the post-handoff notes.

rotation-bot: HANDOFF NOTE: maya -> tom at 2223456789. Primary: tom. Secondary: sasha. Coverage window: 08:00-16:00 UTC.

sasha: I'm secondary. I'll take on followup ticket creation and the retrospective invite.

tom: grabbing the runbook now — embeddings latency runbook: https://redwood.docs/runbooks/embeddings_latency. Initial steps I ran: check queue depth, check GPU utilization, check prefix cache hit rate.

maya: pushed two quick checks I ran:
```
# check KV cache metrics
curl -s http://metrics.internal/cache/hits?env=eu-west-1 | jq .
# check GPU queues
ssh gpu-router-12 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u --delay=1 --count=3'
```
No obvious OOMs or CUDA errors.

tom: thanks. I'll increase KV cache retention on the primary pool by 30% as a short-term mitigation and watch for memory pressure. If that doesn't help within 20m we'll scale up the serving pool by +1 node.

maya: noted. I've created an internal ticket to track mitigations: RED-7632 (Embeddings p99 regression — interim mitigations). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-7632

liam: also created a customer-facing incident note draft for CS: INC-4012. CC: @sasha for wording.

sasha: I'll take INC-4012 and send an update to affected customers once we know if the KV change holds. Also booking a 30m retro tomorrow 09:30 UTC — calendar invite to follow.

maya: action items before I sign off: 1) @tom: apply KV retention bump and report p50/p95/p99 in 15m; 2) @liam: keep the routing tweak if it stays stable; 3) @sasha: open customer update and retro invite; 4) me: update incident timeline & tag logs.

rotation-bot: REMINDER: if handoff includes ongoing incident, please file postmortem ticket template: https://redwood.docs/postmortems/template

tom: KV retention bumped at 2223456875. Observability: p99 improved from 2.1s -> 1.7s in the first 5m. Still above SLA but trending better. CPU on router back down.

maya: great, thanks. If it keeps improving I'll leave the scale decision to @tom to escalate.

liam: routing tweak looks stable, no regressions in throughput.

sasha: created post-handoff followup ticket RED-7633 (Handoff + followup actions for RED-7632). Included checklist and owner assignments. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-7633

maya: final: I'm signing off now. Leaving detailed notes in RED-7632 timeline. @tom you're primary. Ping me if it escalates to P1 or if customer-impact changes. :wave:

rotation-bot: HANDOFF COMPLETE. On-call primary: tom. Secondary: sasha. Shift owner: tom.

tom: thanks @maya. I'm on it. I'll post a short update in 15m with metrics and then hand to next shift as needed.

sasha: adding retro agenda items: root cause hypothesis (long-context jobs), cache tuning recommend, autoscale policy gap, customer comms timing.

tom: posted update at 2223457020: p99 now 1.4s after retention + routing; monitoring for 30m. Will escalate to scaling if it creeps back.

liam: noted for postmortem: capture long-context query patterns and whether we can detect and reroute them proactively.

maya: thanks all — leaving thread. Good handoff. :thumbsup:
